2. The facts of the case, in short, are that Kushal Mondal, predecessor of the respondents herein as plaintiff filed Other Class Suit No. 275 of 1975 in the Court of the then Munsif (now Assistant Judge), Rajshahi for declaration of title to the suit land. The plaintiff stated, inter alia, that the suit land originally belonged to one Askar Mondal, who possessed the same and died leaving behind his brother's son Saber Mondal. Saber Mondal during his lifetime used to possess the suit land and after his death his heir, the original plaintiff Kushal Mondal as his son inherited the property. During S.A. operation, the land in dispute was correctly recorded in the name of the plaintiff and, accordingly, he paid rent to the Government and the Government after accepting him as tenant granted rent receipts in his favour. During R.S. operation, the suit land was erroneously recorded in the name of the defendants. Accordingly, the plaintiffs title to the suit property was doused. Hence, the plaintiff filed the suit. 

 3. The defendants contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material statements made in the plaint. Their case, in short, is that the disputed property originally belonged to Askar Mondal. But during his lifetime, he surrendered the same in favour of ex-landlord, who settled the same to one Chhoto Babu Mondal, who died leaving behind defendant Nos.1 and 4 as daughters and one Saira Bewa as wife. Saira Bewa gifted her share in favour of her grandsons, defendant Nos.2 and 3 and one Rahim Uddin Mondal, Rahim Uddin Mondal died leaving behind defendant No.5 as father and defendant No4 as mother. Accordingly, defendant Nos.1-5 had been possessing the suit land after acquiring the same and paid rent to the Government. The R.S. record of the sit property has correctly been published in the names of defendant and possession in the suit land and as such, the suit was liable to be dismissed. 

 IV. That R.S. operation is done under section 144(A) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and it has got presumptive and evidentiary value of correctness but the High Court Division wrongly held that it has got no presumptive value and as such, arrived at a wrong decision and consequently, the impugned judgment and order is liable to be set aside; and 

 6. Mr. Md. Ali Reza, learned Advocate appearing for respondent Nos.1(a)(i)- 1(a)(vii) and 1(b)-1(e) made submissions in support of the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division. He also submitted that Askar Mondal died leaving Saber Mondal as brother's son who inherited the property left behind by Askar Mondal and subsequently Saber Mondal died leaving son Kushal Mondal and the High Court Division rightly found that Saber Mondal possessed the suit land for more than 12(twelve) years and the S.A. record was duly prepared in the name of the son of Suber Mondal and he paid rents to the Government and, accordingly, the High Court Division rightly made the Rule absolute. He further submitted that all the P.Ws. categorically proved that the plaintiff is owning and possessing the suit land and the S.A. khatian was rightly prepared in the name of the plaintiff and the defendants miserably failed to prove the basis of the recording of the R.S. khatian in respect of the suit land in their names and accordingly the High Court Division disbelieved the case of the defendants and rightly made the Rule absolute which calls for no interference by this Division. He submitted that the defendants have miserably failed to prove that the original owner of the suit land namely Askar Mondal surrendered the suit land in favour of the ex-landlord and the defendants failed to adduce any documentary evidence and also failed to examine any pertinent witness to prove this issue and as such, the High Court Division has rightly made the Rule absolute which calls for no interference by this Division. He submitted that the defendants have failed to prove by adducing any documentary evidence that after surrender of the suit land by Askar Mondal, when the ex-landlord took the same in his khas possession and also when he settled the same to Chhoto Babu Mondal (the predecessor-in-interest of defendant No.1-5), and the trial Court and the High Court Division rightly found that that the defendants miserably failed to prove their case and, therefore, the High Court Division rightly made the Rule absolute which calls for no interference by this Division. He submitted that P.V1s.4 and 5 are independent witnesses who clearly stated in the deposition that the plaintiff has been possessing the suit land and they have land near the suit land and that the High Court Division rightly believed the evidentiary value of the deposition of these two independent witnesses and observed that the witnesses of the defendants contradicted themselves in their depositions in respect of possession of the suit land their testimony is not cogent and credible and, therefore the High Court Division rightly made the Rule absolute which calls for no interference by this Division. He also submitted that the Court of appeal below, as the final Court of fact, did not discuss and consider a single witness examined by the contesting parties while reversing the judgment of the trial Court as is required by Order XLI Rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure. He lastly submitted that the High Court Division as well as the trial Court rightly came to a finding that the plaintiff proved his title and possession in the suit land and the defendants have miserably failed to prove their title and possession in the suit land and hence the impugned judgment calls for no interference by this Division. 

 8.
